question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-declaration ownership with narrowly defined monotonic exceptions as the permanent authority model for opt-in managed configuration layers?
rationale: Tests and lifecycle proof can validate the implementation, but they cannot decide which configuration source should hold lasting authority over security-sensitive paths or whether layered mode should reject runtime writes.

options.title: Approve narrow V1
options.body: Accept the startup-only opt-in contract, require ordinary no-flag compatibility, and coordinate the RFC with the linked implementation.

options.title: Revise authority semantics
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft while precedence, monotonic exceptions, or write behavior are changed and re-proven.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Do not add managed composition to OpenClaw core and retain host-side effective-config generation.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow V1
recommendation.body: Accept the startup-only opt-in contract, require ordinary no-flag compatibility, and coordinate the RFC with the linked implementation.
